kept.heading: DOUBLE-DIGIT ECOMMERCE GROWTH RETURNS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: US ecommerce sales grew 12.2% YoY to $340.2B in Q2 2026, marking a second straight quarter of double-digit growth and outpacing overall retail growth of 6.7%. Ecommerce now accounts for 17.1% of retail sales. Growth varied sharply by category, with general merchandise up 21.6% while clothing rose just 3.8%. The acceleration suggests renewed ecommerce momentum, though inflation and Amazon's earlier Prime Day may have boosted Q2 figures.

kept.heading: IS THE ERA OF THE 15,000 PLUS MARKETING TECHNOLOGY LANDSCAPE COMING TO AN END? (21 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Consolidating a martech stack is less about cutting applications and more about whether each tool provides unique value a broader platform cannot. AI is making many single-purpose tools redundant by combining functions that once required separate systems. However, over-consolidation risks vendor lock-in and losing specialized capabilities. The likely outcome is a smaller core of shared platforms, with specialized tools kept only when they add clear value.

kept.heading: HOW LONG SHOULD BRANDS TEST A CREATOR PARTNERSHIP? 28 CREATOR ECONOMY EXPERTS WEIGH IN (17 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands should test creator partnerships broadly, then give creators 3-6 months or at least three activations to prove repeatability. A single post measures content performance, not the partnership, while short attribution windows can undercount conversions by 40-60%. Match evaluation to the goal and sales cycle, then shift budget toward creators showing brand fit and long-term potential.

kept.heading: YOUR BEST CUSTOMERS MAY NOT BE YOUR MOST ENGAGED (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: More engagement doesn't always mean more value. The right lifecycle strategy starts by defining what healthy usage looks like for each product. A dating app may succeed when users leave, while a utility product may only need monthly use. Customer replies can also reveal intent that clicks and opens miss. As automation makes it easier to build and launch more campaigns, teams need stronger QA and guardrails to manage the added complexity.

kept.heading: META'S AI-FIRST AD BUYING IS FORCING A NEW OPERATING MODEL FOR PAID SOCIAL TEAMS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta's AI-first ad buying is reducing the need for manual campaign optimization and shifting paid social teams toward managing the inputs that guide the system. Clean conversion signals become critical because they shape how Meta optimizes campaigns. Creative production also becomes a bigger performance lever as targeting gets automated. Teams will need to rethink workflows and governance as fewer campaign decisions remain under direct human control.

kept.heading: SAAS DATA MOATS: WHY PROPRIETARY DATA IS THE STRONGEST COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE IN 2026 (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: As AI makes software features easier to replicate, proprietary data is becoming a stronger competitive moat. The advantage comes from data that is unique and improves the product with each customer interaction. A data flywheel can make this advantage compound as more usage creates better insights. However, data only becomes a moat at sufficient scale and with strong governance. Otherwise, it can become an expensive liability rather than a defensible advantage.

kept.heading: SERVED VS SEEN: WHICH BRAND ARE YOU? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands are optimizing for impressions and media efficiency while business growth declines. Being served an ad doesn't mean it was seen or remembered. Test creative organically on social platforms before investing in paid media, then put spend behind content that has already proven it can earn attention.

kept.heading: MARKETERS, THE FREE TOKEN LUNCH IS OVER. IS YOUR STACK READY? (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI costs are changing as models use more tokens for reasoning and companies deploy them across more tasks. The biggest model isn't always the most economical choice. Simple decisions can use cheaper models, while complex problems may justify higher-cost reasoning models. The key metric is shifting from token price to the cost of getting the right answer. AI stacks need to match each task with the right model, rather than defaulting to one model for everything.

kept.heading: “THANKS FOR YOUR QUICK RESPONSE” (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Quick responses show thoughtfulness, helping brands stand out beyond price.

kept.heading: BEHIND JACK IN THE BOX'S PUSH INTO COLLECTIBLES (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Collectible merch has become its own acquisition channel for quick-service brands.

kept.heading: INSTAGRAM SAYS CAPTIONS MATTER. THE REAL SHIFT IS CONTEXT (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The caption is no longer supporting copy on Instagram: it is becoming the context layer that tells people and search engines what a post actually means. The same photo could be a new release, an archival find, or a personal memory, and the caption is what tells the difference once content travels beyond a creator's own followers. Public posts from professional accounts can now be indexed by external search engines, so captions increasingly shape how content gets found.

kept.heading: BRANDS ARE PAYING TO GET INTO AI ANSWERS. PUBLISHERS ARE DELETING THE PAGES THAT PUT THEM THERE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: As search traffic declines, publishers are removing sponsored articles from their archives and charging brands to restore them. This creates a new risk for paid content, especially as those pages can also influence AI search visibility. Brands should negotiate retention terms upfront and regularly audit placements to catch removals early. Dated snapshots can also provide evidence if content disappears.

kept.heading: AUTO-TRANSLATE WON'T WIN EU SHOPPERS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Auto translation can make an ecommerce site readable, but human localization is needed to make it credible and convert shoppers. CSA Research found that 40% of consumers would not buy from a website in a foreign language, while only 20% of Germans and 13% of Poles bought from sellers in other EU countries in 2024. Brands should start with one or two high potential markets, localize product and transactional content, and use native speakers to review sales critical pages, checkout, returns, and emails. Track conversion, search traffic, and engagement by market to identify localization gaps and decide where to expand.

kept.heading: COPYWRITING FRIDAY: DUMB WAYS TO DIE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The “Dumb Ways to Die” campaign shows that unwelcome messages can perform better when audiences are given a reason to engage before receiving the actual ask. Metro Trains Melbourne turned a safety warning into an entertaining music video that reached more than 340 million people, then delivered the safety message only at the end. Marketers can apply the same approach by leading with delight, using memorable rhymes, and replacing abstract claims with vivid, specific details that create mental images. The broader lesson is to make people want to consume the message instead of simply making an unwanted message louder.

kept.heading: HAS GOOGLE DEMOTED LISTICLES? (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google has not broadly demoted listicles, but it has reduced their presence in top search positions, especially lower quality examples. Listicles still appeared in the top 10 for 55.1% of 60,000 queries, but their share of the top three fell from 35.9% to 39.0% in January to 32.0% to 33.0% in August. Self-promoting brand listicles remain common in B2B software, appearing in 46.2% of relevant top 10 results, but 62% of vendor listicles gained estimated organic traffic since January. The bigger issue is declining click opportunity, since 92% of SERPs with a top 10 listicle also included Reddit or YouTube and 93.4% of B2B listicle queries had AI Overviews.

kept.heading: DISPLAY & VIDEO ADS BENCHMARKS 2026: EXCLUSIVE DATA & INSIGHTS FOR EVERY INDUSTRY (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks show that display ad CTRs remain low, ranging from 0.12% for Restaurants & Food to 0.40% for Education & Instruction, while CPCs range from $1.65 to $5.58 across industries. On the USA TODAY Network, high-impact ads averaged 62% viewability and a 0.26% CTR, while video ads averaged 71% viewability, a 0.09% CTR, and a 67% completion rate. Native ads performed better on clicks, averaging a 0.28% CTR and 70% viewability. The data comes from 7,074 LocaliQ display campaigns and 55,798 USA TODAY Network campaigns.

kept.heading: WHICH MARKETING METRIC SHOULD YOU ACTUALLY TRUST? (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Stop looking for one measurement source of truth and instead assign each method a specific decision. MMM should guide strategic budget allocation, incrementality should test whether campaigns create causal lift, and attribution and platform data should support day-to-day optimization. Conflicting results should trigger investigation rather than averaging the numbers, since gaps can reveal flawed assumptions or show that a channel captures existing demand rather than creates new demand. The strongest approach creates a feedback loop where MMM identifies opportunities, experiments test them, and the resulting evidence improves future planning and execution.

kept.heading: SEO IS THE NEW CLEANUP CREW FOR ORGANIZATIONAL DYSFUNCTION (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: SEO teams often become the cleanup crew for problems across the business, from technical debt to unclear messaging and poor customer feedback. Their cross-functional view helps expose these issues, but repeatedly fixing them creates dependency instead of solving the root cause. Recurring problems should move to the teams that own them, with processes that prevent them from returning. The real measure is what stops breaking, not how many issues SEO fixes.

kept.heading: SHOULD YOU BUILD YOUR OWN AUDIENCE STACK IN THE AI ERA? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI has made it much easier to build audience-platform features, but it hasn't eliminated the complexity of running them reliably. Building in-house still means maintaining integrations, sender reputation, and compliance over time. The decision should depend on whether a company has the resources to support the system long term, not just whether it can build the software cheaply. For many publishers, buying the infrastructure may still make more sense.

kept.heading: MBA METRICS FOR SEO: HOW TO SPEAK LEADERSHIP'S LANGUAGE (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Leadership doesn't distrust SEO - it distrusts metrics reported in a language it was never trained to read. Rankings and traffic clicks mean nothing to a team that judges channels by market share and ROI, so the fix is translating SEO into those same terms. Share of Voice stands in for market share, organic traffic value stands in for revenue growth, and branded search volume stands in for brand demand. Reported this way, SEO stops being a marketing activity that needs defending and starts reading like a business one.

kept.heading: META SETTLES SOCIAL MEDIA ADDICTION CASE WITH CALIFORNIA, OTHER STATES FOR $16.7 BILLION (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta's settlement doesn't just bind Meta. States are set to keep 70% of the $16.7 billion payout regardless, but the remaining 30% only unlocks if Google's YouTube and TikTok adopt the same kind of daily time limits, age-assurance checks, and night mode Meta is now required to build. That structure effectively uses Meta's settlement to pressure its rivals into matching child-safety changes without suing them directly.

kept.heading: WHEN AI ANSWER ENGINES QUOTE A PERSON, THAT PERSON IS ON LINKEDIN 74% OF THE TIME (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Individual employees, not company pages, are what AI answer engines cite when they quote a named opinion. Named posts made up 32.8% of social citations across an audit of 63 B2B companies, compared with just 6.7% for company pages, and the person quoted had published on LinkedIn 74% of the time. A model needs a name and title to attach to a claim, something a brand page speaking in aggregate can't offer the same way.

kept.heading: THE 5 MOST EFFECTIVE LINKEDIN ADS TACTICS IN Q3 2026 (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Pair LinkedIn Audience Network with highly targeted third-party audiences to expand reach, turn customer wins into ungated case study document ads, and gate high-value offers when ungated content falls flat. Thought leader ads with preview links can drive more inbound, while branded single-image TLAs can combine strong engagement with brand building.

kept.heading: THE NEW DEMAND GEN MANAGER SUCCESS KIT (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A guide for demand gen leaders navigating their first 90 days. It covers how to assess the business, launch campaigns quickly, build the right measurement infrastructure, and identify high-value audience signals. It also shows where AI can streamline daily workflows without replacing strategic judgment.

kept.heading: THE 4 ROLES EVERY MODERN MEASUREMENT FUNCTION NEEDS AND ALMOST NO COMPANY HAS STAFFED ALL 4 (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Modern marketing measurement needs four distinct roles: measurement scientist, experimentation lead, finance translator, and decision architect. The scientist builds trustworthy models, the experimentation lead produces causal evidence, and the finance translator reconciles modeled impact with financial results so finance can trust the numbers. The decision architect connects those findings to budget processes by defining decision rights, timing, and override protocols. Combining roles may work temporarily, but understaffing usually leaves the relationship and decision work undone and turns measurement back into a modeling exercise.

kept.heading: BEFORE DECLARING “_ _ _ IS DEAD”, CONSIDER THAT YOU MAY JUST BE BORING (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Marketers and creators often mistake their own feeds for market research, declaring trends “dead” when they're really just tired of seeing them. Algorithmic feeds create highly personalized views of culture, so repeated exposure can make a format feel saturated even when other audiences are still discovering it. Before writing off a trend, look beyond your own feed and separate personal fatigue from actual audience behavior.

kept.heading: THE GREAT META MIGRATION (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta's ad playbook is spreading well beyond Meta, with alumni now running ad product and sales at OpenAI, Amazon, TikTok, and Roku, all chasing the same self-serve formula that took Meta's own ad business past a $1 trillion market cap. Turnover has been fueled by real turmoil inside Meta, including rolling layoffs and morale issues dating back to 2018. The strategy isn't foolproof, since Pinterest brought over a wave of Facebook talent in its early days and it still couldn't replicate Facebook's growth curve.

kept.heading: BOOTS' REACTIVE MARKETING STRATEGY CAPITALIZES ON INFLUENCER'S IDEA TO GIVE BACK TO ARIANA GRANDE FANS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Boots turned a creator's TikTok idea into a $10K Ariana Grande concert activation within hours, inviting 22 fans to the show. The move generated more than 793K views across related creator content and sparked positive brand sentiment. The activation shows the value of giving social teams freedom to act quickly when relevant opportunities emerge. It also highlights growing audience fatigue with brands taking influencers to high-demand events instead of genuine fans.

kept.heading: GOOGLE EXPANDS DIRECT BOOKING FOR LOCAL SERVICES ADS (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Businesses no longer have to manually link a booking partner.
